questions.questionText: Three bags contain a total of 24 apples. The first and the second bag contain a total of 11 apples. The second and the third bag contain a total of 18 apples. How many apples are there in the first and third bags?
hints: If you know the first + second bags together, then total − (first + second) tells you the third bag alone.
Total − (two bags) = the bag that was left out.

questions.questionText: The number of whole numbers that lie between 4² and 4³ is:
hints: First work out 4² and 4³. 'Between' means you do NOT count the two end numbers.
Whole numbers strictly between a and b = (b − a) − 1.

questions.questionText: A watch keeps exact time, but it has only the hour hand. When the hour hand is 4/5 of the distance between 12 and 1, the correct time is:
hints: The hour hand takes one full hour (60 minutes) to go from 12 to 1. So 4/5 of the way means 4/5 of 60 minutes.
Fraction of a distance = same fraction of the time taken.

stepByStep.text: From 12 to 1 the hour hand takes 60 minutes.

questions.questionText: The number 36 is 12% of which number?
hints: If 12% of a number is 36, what is 1% of it? Then find 100%.
Find 1% first, then multiply by 100.

questions.questionText: A worker is paid Rs.3 per hour up to 40 hours. Overtime is twice the payment for regular time. If he is paid Rs.168, how many hours of overtime did he work?
hints: First find what he earns for the regular 40 hours. The money left over is overtime pay, and overtime pays Rs.6 each hour.
Overtime rate = 2 × Rs.3 = Rs.6 per hour. Hours = money ÷ rate per hour.

questions.questionText: What is the value of the tenth term 'T' in the sequence: 2, 7, 14, 23, 34, … 'T'
hints: Find the gaps between terms: 5, 7, 9, 11 … The gaps themselves go up by 2. Keep extending until you reach the 10th term.
When gaps form a pattern, extend the gaps: 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17, 19, 21.

questions.questionText: Find the value of 'x' in the equation 3x − 4(x + 6) = 0
hints: Open the bracket first: multiply 4 by BOTH x and 6. Then collect the x terms.
Distribute: 4(x + 6) = 4x + 24. Then solve the balance.

questions.questionText: A boy played for 1 hr 15 min. Which decimal fraction represents the time he played for?
hints: There are 60 minutes in an hour, not 100. What fraction of an hour is 15 minutes? Then change the fraction to a decimal.
15 minutes = 15/60 hour = ¼ hour = 0.25 hour.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the H.C.F. of 18, 24 and 36?
hints: HCF is the greatest number that divides ALL three numbers exactly. Test the options on 18 first, then check them on 24 and 36.
HCF = biggest common factor. Use prime factors: 18 = 2×3×3, 24 = 2×2×2×3, 36 = 2×2×3×3.

questions.questionText: Which of the following fractions is greater than 1/3 but less than 7/8?
hints: Change everything into 24ths. 1/3 and 7/8 both fit into 24ths.
Common denominator: LCM of 3, 8 and the option denominators → 24.

stepByStep.text: 1/3 = 8/24 and 7/8 = 21/24. We need a fraction between 8/24 and 21/24.

questions.questionText: Amar walks a certain distance from A to B and rides back from B to A taking a total time of 37 minutes. He could walk both ways A to B and B to A in 55 minutes. How long will it take Amar to ride both ways?
hints: Walking both ways takes 55 min, so walking ONE way takes half of that. Then ride one way = 37 − walk one way.
Walk one way + ride one way = 37 min. Walk one way = 55 ÷ 2.

questions.questionText: A fruit seller bought 4 dozens of oranges at Rs.12 per dozen and 2 dozen of oranges at Rs.16 per dozen. He sold them all to earn 20% profit. At what price per dozen did he sell the oranges?
hints: Find the total cost of all the oranges and the number of dozens. Add 20% to the cost to get the total selling price, then share it per dozen.
SP = CP × 120 ÷ 100 for 20% profit.

questions.questionText: The length of one side of the rectangle is 8 cm and its perimeter is 40 cm. Find the area of the rectangle.
hints: Perimeter = 2 × (L + B). Half of 40 gives L + B. Then find the other side.
L + B = Perimeter ÷ 2. Area = L × B.

questions.questionText: How many natural numbers below 2009 are divisible by both 4 and 6?
hints: Numbers divisible by both 4 and 6 are multiples of their LCM. Find the LCM, then divide 2008 by it.
Count of multiples of L up to N = N ÷ L (whole part only).

questions.questionText: If 40 gm of talc powder costs Rs.12, what is the cost of 70 gm of talc powder?
hints: Find the cost of just 1 gram first. Then multiply by 70.
Unitary method: find the value of 1, then multiply.

questions.questionText: In one crore how many tens are there?
hints: Write one crore in digits (1 followed by 7 zeros). How many tens fit in it? Divide by 10.

questions.questionText: What will be the place value of the digit 4 in the smallest five-digit odd number formed by using all the given digits only once: 1, 8, 4, 0 and 7?
hints: An odd number must end in 1 or 7. For the SMALLEST number, put small digits at the front (but 0 can't be first). Try both endings.
Smallest number: smallest non-zero digit first, then the rest in increasing order. Last digit must be odd.

stepByStep.text: End in 7: remaining digits 1, 8, 4, 0 → smallest is 10487.
The digit 4 is in the hundreds place → 4 × 100 = 400.

questions.questionText: A vendor bought 6 toffees for a rupee. How many toffees must he sell for a rupee to gain 20%?
hints: Find the cost of 1 toffee. Add 20% to get the selling price of 1 toffee. Then see how many such toffees make Re 1.
SP of 1 = CP of 1 × 120 ÷ 100. Number per rupee = 1 ÷ SP of one.

stepByStep.text: So for Re 1 he must sell 5 toffees.

questions.questionText: What is the sum of: a + b − 1, b − a + 1 and 1 − 2b?
hints: Write all three expressions in one line and remove the brackets. Then cancel the pairs: +a with −a, +b … with −2b …
Combine like terms: put a's together, b's together and plain numbers together.

questions.questionText: Simplify using BODMAS: 8 − 4.2 ÷ 6 + 0.3 × 0.4
hints: Do ÷ and × first (left to right), then + and −. 4.2 ÷ 6 and 0.3 × 0.4 are the first two jobs.
BODMAS: Division and Multiplication come before Addition and Subtraction.

questions.subTopic: Grade 5 — Numbers (place value and number system)
questions.questionText: In the case of how many digits in the number 2138574, their positions in the number and the positions when the digits of the number are arranged in ascending order are identical?
hints: Arrange the digits from smallest to biggest, write that number underneath, and compare position by position.
Line up the two numbers and tick every place where the digits match.

questions.subTopic: Grade 5 — Numbers (place value and number system)
questions.questionText: Mr. Sam's age in the year 2000 was a multiple of 8 and in the year 2001 it was a multiple of 7. In which year was Mr. Sam born?
hints: Test each birth year. Age in 2000 = 2000 − birth year; age in 2001 is one more. Both conditions must work.
Ages in consecutive years differ by 1: we need a multiple of 8 followed by a multiple of 7 (like 48 and 49).

stepByStep.text: 1960 → age 40 (✓ multiple of 8) but 41 is not a multiple of 7 ✗.
1952 → age 48 = 8 × 6 ✓ and next year 49 = 7 × 7 ✓ → born in 1952.

questions.questionText: At Uncle's Cafe the food costs as follows: 1 Toast and 1 Tea cost Rs.4. 2 Toast and 2 Sandwich cost Rs.9. 1 Sandwich and 2 Teas cost Rs.2. What would 1 Toast, 1 Sandwich and 1 Tea together cost?
hints: Halve the second sentence: 1 Toast + 1 Sandwich costs Rs.4.50. Then use Toast + Tea = 4 to work out Toast, Tea and Sandwich one by one.
Use letters: T = toast, S = sandwich, E = tea. T + E = 4, T + S = 4.5, S + 2E = 2.

stepByStep.text: From T + E = 4 → E = 4 − T, and S = 4.5 − T.

questions.questionText: Jim bought a cat and a dog for Rs.600 each. Later he sold them. He made a profit of 20% on the dog but made a loss of 25% on the cat. How much did he get altogether when he sold the cat and the dog?
hints: Work out the selling price of each pet separately: 120% of 600 for the dog and 75% of 600 for the cat. The question asks for the money he GOT, not the profit.
SP with profit = CP × (100 + %) ÷ 100. SP with loss = CP × (100 − %) ÷ 100.
Make all the fractions have the same bottom number (denominator). The LCM of 2, 4, 3 and 6 is 12.
Same denominator first, then add/subtract only the numerators.

questions.questionText: What term fits in the blank space in the sequence: 1/2, 4, 1/8, 16, ____, 64
hints: Two patterns are mixed together. Look at the 1st, 3rd, 5th terms on their own, and the 2nd, 4th, 6th on their own.
Alternate-term series: split into two simple series.

questions.questionText: Of the given expressions, which expression has the least value?
hints: Work out each one with BODMAS: brackets first, then × before + and −.
BODMAS: Brackets → Multiplication → Addition/Subtraction.

questions.questionText: At the end of season sale a shirt costing Rs.700 is sold for Rs.651. What was the discount percent?
hints: Discount = marked price − sale price. Then discount % = discount ÷ marked price × 100.
Discount % = (Discount ÷ Original price) × 100.

questions.questionText: A man bought 27 eggs. How many dozen eggs did he buy (express in decimals)?
hints: 1 dozen = 12 eggs. Divide 27 by 12 and write the answer as a decimal.
Number of dozens = number of items ÷ 12.

questions.questionText: If 12 buckets can hold 108 litres of water, how many buckets will be required to store 162 litres of water?
hints: Find how many litres ONE bucket holds. Then see how many such buckets are needed for 162 litres.
Unitary method: litres per bucket = total ÷ number of buckets.

questions.questionText: Mrs. Joshi bought five gifts A, B, C, D and E for a total of Rs.21. For A and B she paid a total of Rs.6. For B and C she paid a total of Rs.10. For C and D she paid a total of Rs.7. For D and E she paid a total of Rs.9. What is the price for gifts A and E together?
hints: A + B and C + D together use up 4 gifts. The only gift not included is E. Use the total of all 5 gifts.
Total of all five = 21. (A + B) + (C + D) leaves E out.

questions.questionText: Three times the measure of an angle is the measure of its supplement. What is the measure of the angle?
hints: Supplement of an angle x is 180° − x. Write 'three times the angle = its supplement' as a balance.
Supplementary angles add up to 180°. Here: 3x = 180° − x.

stepByStep.text: Let the angle be x. Supplement = 180° − x.

questions.questionText: The three sides of a triangle are (2a + 6) cm, (3a + 5) cm and (a + 7) cm. What is the perimeter of the triangle if the value of a = 3?
hints: Put a = 3 into each side to get three lengths. Perimeter means add all three sides.
Perimeter of a triangle = sum of its three sides.

questions.questionText: At the rate of 10% p.a. S.I., what sum of money will amount to Rs.4500 in a 5 year period?
hints: Interest for 5 years at 10% a year is 50% of the principal. So the amount is 150% of the principal.
Amount = Principal + SI. SI for 5 years at 10% = 5 × 10% = 50% of P.

questions.subTopic: Grade 5 — Numbers (place value and number system)
questions.questionText: If (f − 9) is an even number, which of the following could be the 25th odd number coming after it?
hints: Try a real number: let f − 9 = 10 (even). Odd numbers after it: 11, 13, 15 … The 25th is 10 + 1 + 24 × 2. Then compare with f.
After an even number e, the 1st odd number is e + 1 and the nth odd number is e + 1 + (n − 1) × 2.

stepByStep.text: 25th odd number after e = e + 1 + (24 × 2) = e + 49.

questions.questionText: The combined age of A and B is 39, B and C is 40, C and D is 38 and D and E is 44. The total of the ages of all the five is 105. Which of the following can be the age of the youngest member of the given five?
hints: Use the total of all five (105). If you take away two pairs, the one person left over is easy to find. Then work out the others one at a time.
Total of all five − (two pairs that don't overlap) = the one person left out.

stepByStep.text: Ages: A 21, B 18, C 22, D 16, E 28 → youngest is 16.

questions.questionText: A water tank is 5/6 full. When 30 litres of water are removed from the tank, the tank is 4/5 full. How much water does the tank hold when full?
hints: The 30 litres removed is the DIFFERENCE between the two fractions. Subtract 5/6 − 4/5 (use 30 as the common denominator).
If a fraction of the whole is a known amount, whole = amount ÷ fraction.

questions.questionText: A wholesaler allows a discount of 20% on the list price to a retailer. The retailer sells at 8% discount on the list price. The profit % of the retailer is:
hints: Pick an easy list price like Rs.100. What does the retailer PAY (after 20% off)? What does the retailer RECEIVE (after 8% off)?
Profit % = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100. Choose list price = 100 to make it easy.

questions.questionText: A clock is showing 11:00 a.m. now. When the hour hand has turned through 165°, what will be the time?
hints: The hour hand turns 30° in every hour. How many hours is 165°?
Hour hand: 30° per hour. Hours passed = angle ÷ 30.

questions.questionText: The sum of the ages of four children, Anil, Bunty, Chetan and David is 20. David is 5 years older than Chetan, and 3 years older than Bunty. Anil is 3 years younger than Chetan. How old is Anil?
hints: Write everyone's age in terms of Chetan's age. Then add all four and set it equal to 20.
Pick one person as the base (Chetan = c), express others using c, then solve.

stepByStep.text: Chetan = c. David = c + 5. Bunty = David − 3 = c + 2. Anil = c − 3.

questions.questionText: A seagull travelled 16500 miles from Finland to Australia. It travelled at a rate of 125 miles per day. In how many days did the seagull reach Australia?
hints: Time = Distance ÷ Speed. Try dividing 16500 by 125 — or divide both by 25 first to make it easier.
Time = Distance ÷ Speed.

questions.questionText: A piece of work can be done by 72 men in 40 hours. How many hours will 9 men take to complete the same work?
hints: Fewer men take MORE time. Total work = men × hours stays the same. 9 men is how many times fewer than 72 men?
Men × Hours = constant (inverse proportion).

stepByStep.text: (72 men is 8 times 9 men, so 8 times the time: 40 × 8 = 320 ✓)

questions.questionText: What will be the simple interest on Rs.3000 at 12% p.a. for 5 years?
hints: Use SI = P × R × T ÷ 100. 1% of 3000 is Rs.30.

questions.questionText: Which set of signs of operations should be replaced in the boxes so that the equation is true: 10 □ 6 □ 4 □ 6 = 28
hints: Try each option using BODMAS: multiply/divide first, then add/subtract.
Test each option one by one.

questions.questionText: A clock was on sale last month for Rs.10800, but this month its price was reduced to Rs.8640. What percentage discount is this?
hints: Find how many rupees the price dropped by. Then compare with the OLD price: drop ÷ old price × 100.
Discount % = (Discount ÷ Original price) × 100.

questions.questionText: How many two-digit numbers are there which are divisible by 2, 3 and 4?
hints: A number divisible by 2, 3 and 4 is a multiple of their LCM. Find the LCM, then list the two-digit multiples.
LCM of 2, 3, 4 = 12. List multiples of 12 between 10 and 99.

questions.questionText: A man bought 21 oranges. Which of the following decimals represents the same?
hints: 1 dozen = 12. Divide 21 by 12 and write as a decimal. 21 ÷ 12 = 1 and 9 left over...
Number of dozens = number of items ÷ 12.
Start from the INNERMOST bracket ( ), then { }, then [ ]. Do 6 ÷ 2 outside separately.
Bracket order: ( ) → { } → [ ]. Then BODMAS.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a perfect square number?
hints: Find the square roots nearby: 100² = 10000 and 105² = 11025. Check which numbers land exactly.
A perfect square has a whole number square root. Use 100² = 10000, 101² = 10201.

questions.questionText: In how many years will Rs.2000 amount to Rs.3500 at simple interest of 5% p.a.?
hints: Amount − Principal = interest. Find how much interest comes each year (5% of 2000), then divide.

questions.questionText: The perimeter of a square and an equilateral triangle are the same. If the side of the triangle is 8 cm, then the side of the square is:
hints: Find the triangle's perimeter (3 equal sides). Share that perimeter equally among the 4 sides of the square.
Equilateral triangle = 3 × side. Square = 4 × side.

questions.questionText: The breadth of a rectangle is half the length of the rectangle. If the perimeter of the rectangle is 48 cm, then its area is:
hints: If breadth = 1 part, length = 2 parts. Perimeter = 2 × (L + B) = 2 × 3 parts. Find one part first.
Perimeter = 2(L + B). Area = L × B.

questions.questionText: If 2x + 1 = 8, then 4x + 1 = ?
hints: You don't need x. 4x is double 2x. First find 2x from the equation.

questions.questionText: In 1976 it was estimated that there were 250000 lions in Africa. Over the past 40 years this figure has decreased by 90%. What is the current estimate for the number of lions in Africa?
hints: If 90% are gone, what percent are LEFT? Find that percent of 250000. (Don't pick 225000 — that's the number that disappeared.)
Remaining % = 100% − decrease %.

questions.questionText: A worker gets Rs.504 for 7 days of work. How many days should he work to get Rs.792?
hints: Find the pay for ONE day first. Then see how many days make Rs.792.
Unitary method: 1 day's pay = total ÷ days.

questions.questionText: A man is cycling towards the North-East direction. He turns to his left and is now cycling towards West direction. How many degrees to his left did he turn?
hints: Turning LEFT means anticlockwise. Go from North-East to North, then North-West, then West, counting 45° each step.
Each step between neighbouring directions (N, NE, E …) is 45°.

questions.questionText: What is the value of: (2/3 + 1/3)/(2/3 − 1/3)
hints: Work out the top and the bottom separately. The fraction line means 'top ÷ bottom'.
Add/subtract fractions with the same denominator by combining numerators.

questions.questionText: A two-digit number ♣9 is multiplied by a three-digit number ♣♣3. The digits in the ♣ place are not necessarily the same. Which of the following can be the product of the given two numbers?
hints: Check the LAST digit first (9 × 3). Then check the smallest and largest possible products to rule out options that are too small or too big.
Smallest product = 19 × 103 = 1957. Largest product = 99 × 993 = 98,307.

stepByStep.text: Last digit: 9 × 3 = 27 → ends in 7 (all options end in 7, so size must decide).
1907 and 957 are smaller than the smallest possible product 1957 ✗.
756927 is bigger than the largest possible product (about 98,300) ✗.

hints: Count the decimal places: 2.1 has 1 and 0.24 has 2. Put that many decimal places in 504.
Decimal places in the answer = total decimal places in the numbers multiplied.

stepByStep.text: 2.1 has 1 decimal place, 0.24 has 2 → total 3 decimal places.

questions.questionText: Dog A barks every 5 minutes, Dog B barks every 8 minutes and Dog C barks every 12 minutes. They started barking at 11:30 p.m. and continued barking the whole night. Later that night Mr. John woke up when the three dogs barked at the same time (making a very loud noise). What time did Mr. John wake up?
hints: They bark together again after the LCM of 5, 8 and 12 minutes. Then add that time to 11:30 p.m.
LCM tells when repeating events happen together again.

questions.subTopic: Grade 5 — Numbers (place value and number system)
questions.questionText: If (x + 37) is an even number, then the 17th odd number coming after it is represented by:
hints: Try a real even number, say 10. The odd numbers after it are 11, 13, 15 … What is the 17th one? Compare with 10.
After an even number e: nth odd number = e + 1 + (n − 1) × 2.

stepByStep.text: 17th odd number after e = e + 1 + (16 × 2) = e + 33.

questions.questionText: A motorcycle is moving at the rate of 30 m/s. Its speed in km/hr is:
hints: To change m/s into km/h multiply by 18 ÷ 5 (or by 3.6).

questions.questionText: The length of a rectangle is (4a + 3b) and the breadth is (3a − b). Find its perimeter.
hints: First add the length and breadth (combine like terms). Then multiply by 2.
Perimeter = 2 × (L + B).

questions.questionText: A dozen pencils cost Rs.18. How much would you pay for 18 pencils?
hints: 1 dozen = 12 pencils. Find the cost of one pencil first.
Unitary method: find the value of 1.
Add up the four numbers on the top, then add up the four numbers at the bottom. Then divide the top total by the bottom total.
Add the numbers on top, add the numbers at the bottom, then divide.

questions.subTopic: Grade 5 — Numbers (place value and number system)
questions.questionText: Form the greatest odd number using the digits 7, 5, 2, 0 and 4 each only once.
hints: An odd number must END in an odd digit (7 or 5). For the greatest number the biggest digits must come first. Compare ending in 5 and ending in 7.
Greatest number: biggest digits at the front. Odd: last digit odd.

stepByStep.text: End with 5: the rest 7, 4, 2, 0 arranged greatest → 74205.
(75420 is even, so it can't be the answer.)

questions.questionText: The least number that should be subtracted from 370 so that the resulting number is a square number is:
hints: Find the biggest perfect square that is less than 370. 19² and 20² are close.
Subtract the number from the nearest perfect square BELOW it.

stepByStep.text: 19² = 361 and 20² = 400. The square just below 370 is 361.

questions.questionText: In the series 1, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, … what will be the units digit of the 30th term of the series?
hints: Compare the terms with powers of 2: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64. How does each term relate? Then look at the pattern of last digits of powers of 2.
nth term = 2ⁿ − 1. Last digits of 2ⁿ repeat every 4: 2, 4, 8, 6.

questions.questionText: What will be the quotient when 12xy + 8y is divided by 4y?
hints: Divide EACH part separately by 4y: 12xy ÷ 4y and 8y ÷ 4y. Divide the numbers and cancel the letters.
(a + b) ÷ c = a ÷ c + b ÷ c.

questions.questionText: A train 200 m long passes a pole in 9 seconds. The speed of the train in km/hr is:
hints: Passing a pole means covering its own length (200 m). Find the speed in m/s, then change to km/h (× 18/5).
Speed = Distance ÷ Time. m/s → km/h: × 18/5.

questions.questionText: In which of the following numbers is the digit in the tens place exactly four times the digit in the thousands place?
hints: For each number, find the thousands digit (1st) and tens digit (3rd). Is the tens digit exactly 4 times the thousands digit?
Thousands = 1st digit of a 4-digit number. Tens = 3rd digit.

questions.questionText: The perimeter of a square ground is 120 m. What is its area?
hints: Find one side first (perimeter ÷ 4). Then area = side × side.
Square: perimeter = 4 × side, area = side × side.

questions.questionText: If 1 gram of grass seeds is needed to plant 1 sq. metre, how much grass seed will be needed to plant an entire field that is 110 metres long and 70 metres wide?
hints: Find the area of the field first (length × width). Each sq. metre needs 1 gram. Then change grams into kilograms (÷ 1000).
Area of rectangle = L × B. 1000 grams = 1 kg.

questions.questionText: If the digit 2 is placed in between the digits 3 and 5 of the number 43541, by how much is the new number more than the previous number?
hints: Write the new number first (put 2 between the 3 and the 5), then subtract the old number.
Write both numbers neatly and subtract.

stepByStep.text: Old number = 43541. Putting 2 between 3 and 5 gives 4 3 2 5 4 1 = 432541.

hints: Count how the numbers changed: 1.5 is 15 ÷ 10 and 0.05 is 0.005 × 10. Or just work it out step by step: 1.5 × 0.05 first, then × 100.
Multiplying by 100 moves the decimal point 2 places right.

questions.questionText: The sum of two consecutive odd numbers is 12. Which equation from the following represents the given statement using 'm' as the variable?
hints: Consecutive odd numbers differ by 2. If the first is m, what is the next one? 'Sum' means add them.
Consecutive odd numbers: m, m + 2. Sum → m + (m + 2).

stepByStep.text: First odd number = m. Next odd number = m + 2.
(Product would be m(m + 2); that is not what the question says.)

questions.subTopic: Grade 5 — Numbers (place value and number system)
questions.questionText: A palindrome number is a number which remains the same when read backwards. For example: 707 or 5225. A three-digit palindrome number is added to 2017 to get a 4-digit palindrome number. What is the sum of the digits of the three-digit palindrome number added to 2017?
hints: The answer is between 2118 and 3016, so it starts with 2 (or 3). A palindrome starting with 2 ends with 2. Use the last digit: 7 + (last digit of your number) must end in 2.
A palindrome reads the same both ways (like 2552).

stepByStep.text: The 3-digit palindrome looks like a b a. Last digit: 7 + a must end in 2 → a = 5.
So the number is 5b5. 2017 + 5b5 = 2522 + 10b. We want a palindrome 2yy2.
b = 3 gives 2552 — it reads the same backwards ✓. So the number is 535.

questions.questionText: The given series 13, 16, 19, 22 … is increasing by 3 each time. What will be the 75th number of the series?
hints: nth term = first term + (n − 1) × 3. Remember to use (n − 1), not n.
nth term = a + (n − 1) × d.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: The supplementary angle of an angle is always less than 90°.
The complementary angle of an acute angle is always an acute angle.
The complementary and the supplementary angle of a given angle always sum up to 360°.
All the given statements are false.

hints: Test each statement with an example angle like 30°. Complement = 90° − angle, supplement = 180° − angle.
Acute angle: less than 90°. Complement = 90° − x. Supplement = 180° − x.

stepByStep.text: Statement A: supplement of 30° is 150°, which is more than 90° ✗.
Statement B: if x is acute (between 0° and 90°), 90° − x is also between 0° and 90° → acute ✓.
Statement C: (90 − x) + (180 − x) = 270 − 2x, which isn't always 360° ✗.

questions.questionText: On a number line, point A is at 1/5 and point B is at 1/3. Point C is exactly between point A and B. What fraction could be at C?
hints: The point exactly in the middle is the average of the two fractions: add them, then halve. Make the denominators the same first.
Midpoint = (first + second) ÷ 2.

stepByStep.text: Middle of 3/15 and 5/15 is 4/15 (halfway between 3 and 5 is 4).

questions.questionText: The perimeter of a rectangle is 72 cm. The length and breadth of the rectangle are:
hints: Perimeter = 2 × (L + B), so L + B must be half of 72. Add the two numbers in each option.
L + B = Perimeter ÷ 2.

questions.questionText: Nine men complete a certain work in 32 days, then in how many days will 72 men complete the same work?
hints: More men finish faster. 72 men is how many times 9 men? Then divide the days by that number.
Men × Days = constant (inverse proportion).

questions.questionText: After playing 500 games, Sachin's success rate at Spider Solitaire is 49%. Sachin determines that now on he will win every game. How many extra games does he have to win so that his success rate increases to 50%?
hints: First find how many games he has won so far (49% of 500). Each new game adds 1 win AND 1 to the total. Try the options!
Success rate = wins ÷ games played × 100.

questions.questionText: Yesterday at a museum, 4/5 of the visitors were adults. 120 children visited the museum. 3/8 of the adults were male. How many male adults visited the museum?
hints: If 4/5 are adults, what fraction are children? The 120 children are that fraction of all visitors.
Whole = part ÷ fraction.

questions.questionText: The measure of an angle is (38 − x)°. What will be the measure of the complementary angle of it?
hints: Complementary angles add to 90°. Subtract the angle from 90, and be careful with the minus sign in front of x.
Complement = 90° − angle.

stepByStep.text: Remove the bracket: 90 − 38 + x (minus times minus gives plus).

questions.questionText: The rate of interest a bank offers for deposit is 6% p.a. S.I. What interest will Rs.8000 earn if deposited for 2 years?
hints: Use SI = P × R × T ÷ 100. 1% of 8000 is 80.

questions.questionText: Which of the following will be equal to 100?
hints: Work out each one with BODMAS: brackets first, then multiplication, then + and −.
BODMAS: brackets, then × before + and −.

questions.questionText: The sum of the squares of which two numbers will result in a square number?
hints: Square both numbers in each option, add them, and check whether the total is a perfect square. Remember the famous triple 8, 15, 17!

questions.questionText: The two sides of a square are (3a − 7) cm and (2a − 1) cm. Which of the following can be its perimeter?
hints: All sides of a square are equal, so (3a − 7) = (2a − 1). Solve for a, then find the side and perimeter.
Square: all sides equal. Perimeter = 4 × side.

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper buys 6 dozens of long books. He sold 3 dozen at Rs.150 per dozen and the other 3 dozen at Rs.200 per dozen. Finally he made a profit of Rs.180. At what rate per dozen did he buy the long books?
hints: Find the total he got from selling. Then CP = SP − Profit. Finally share the cost over 6 dozens.
CP = SP − Profit.

questions.questionText: Walking at a speed of 6 km/hr, what distance would he cover in 3 minutes?
hints: How many metres does he walk in 1 hour? Then in 1 minute?
6 km/h = 6000 m in 60 minutes = 100 m per minute.

questions.questionText: How many weeks are there in 8 × 7 × 6 × 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 minutes?
hints: Work out how many minutes there are in ONE week (7 days × 24 hours × 60 minutes). Then divide.
1 week = 7 × 24 × 60 = 10080 minutes.

questions.questionText: Using the digits 9, 5, 0, 7 and 3 each only once the greatest 5-digit number is formed. What is the difference between the place value of the digit 5 and 3 in the number formed?
hints: Greatest number: biggest digit first, then next biggest … Write the number, then find the place value of 5 and 3 in it.
Place value = digit × value of its place.

stepByStep.text: 5 is in the hundreds place → 500. 3 is in the tens place → 30.

hints: Change every fraction into 28ths. 28 is a multiple of 2, 4, 7 and 14.
Use the LCM (28) as the common denominator.

questions.questionText: Find the H.C.F. of 54, 288 and 360.
hints: The HCF must divide all three. Check which options divide 54 first, then test them on 288 and 360.
HCF = greatest common factor. Prime factors: 54 = 2 × 3³, 288 = 2⁵ × 3², 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5.

questions.questionText: After selling 15 dozens of bananas a man gains Rs.45. How many dozens of bananas should he sell so as to gain Rs.84?
hints: Find how much he gains on just ONE dozen. Then divide 84 by that.
Unitary method: gain per dozen = total gain ÷ dozens.

questions.questionText: Find the value of 'a' in 4a − 5 = 2a + 3.
hints: Collect the 'a' terms on one side and the numbers on the other. Change the sign when a term crosses the = sign.
Same operation on both sides keeps the balance.

questions.questionText: Which of the following expressions divides 91abc to get 7c?
hints: Divide the numbers (91 ÷ 7) and cancel the letters that appear both on top and at the bottom.
If X ÷ Y = Z, then Y = X ÷ Z.

stepByStep.text: 91 ÷ 7 = 13. The letter c cancels: abc ÷ c = ab.

questions.questionText: A man bought some articles. Which decimal fraction from the below CANNOT represent the number of articles he bought in dozens?
hints: Articles must be a whole number. Multiply each decimal by 12 — which one gives a number with a decimal part?
Number of articles = dozens × 12 (must be whole).

stepByStep.text: 3.15 × 12 = 37.8 ✗ — you can't have 0.8 of an article.

questions.questionText: The perimeter of an equilateral triangle is (16a + 7b). If a = 2 and b = 4, then the side of the triangle is?
hints: Put a = 2 and b = 4 into the perimeter. An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides.
Side of equilateral triangle = Perimeter ÷ 3.

questions.questionText: An article costing Rs.800 is sold at a discount of 20%. What was its sale price?
hints: Find 20% of 800 (the discount). Then subtract it from 800.
Sale price = Price − Discount. Or 80% of the price.

questions.questionText: In how many years will Rs.4000 double at the rate of 12.5% S.I.?
hints: 'Double' means the interest earned equals the principal (Rs.4000). How much interest does Rs.4000 earn in one year at 12.5%?
T = SI × 100 ÷ (P × R). Here SI = P.

questions.questionText: A three-digit number ♣♣7 is multiplied by a two-digit number ♣8. The digits in ♣ place are not necessarily the same. Which of the following can be the product of the given two numbers?
hints: Check the last digit (7 × 8). Then check the smallest and the biggest possible product to throw out the rest.
Smallest product = 107 × 18 = 1926. Largest product = 997 × 98 = 97,706.

stepByStep.text: Last digit: 7 × 8 = 56 → ends in 6. That removes 29405 (ends in 5).
1906 is smaller than the smallest possible product (1926) ✗.
977706 is bigger than the largest possible product (97,706) ✗.

questions.subTopic: Grade 5 — Numbers (place value and number system)
questions.questionText: If (x + 37) represents an even number, then the 17th odd number prior to it would be?
hints: Try a real even number such as 50. The odd numbers BEFORE it are 49, 47, 45 … (going down). Find the 17th and compare.
Before an even number e: nth odd number prior = e − 1 − (n − 1) × 2.

stepByStep.text: 17th odd number before e = e − 1 − (16 × 2) = e − 33.

questions.questionText: The square of 125 is?
hints: A shortcut for numbers ending in 5: multiply the front digits by (front + 1) and write 25 at the end.
(n5)² = n × (n + 1) followed by 25. For 125: n = 12.

questions.questionText: Each test at a class is for 80 marks. Total 5 tests were to be conducted. A student has scored 30% marks at the first 4 tests. To have a score of 35% marks on 5 tests, how many marks must he score in the 5th test?
hints: Find the total marks of all 5 tests and the marks he needs for 35%. Then find what he already has from the first 4 tests (30% of their total).
Needed in last test = (Target total) − (marks already scored).

stepByStep.text: Total of 5 tests = 5 × 80 = 400. 35% of 400 = 140 marks needed.
First 4 tests total 320 marks; 30% of 320 = 96 scored.

questions.questionText: In what time will a train 100 m long running at a speed of 36 km/hr pass a man standing by the rails?
hints: Change 36 km/h to m/s (× 5/18). The train must travel its own length to pass the man.
Time = Distance ÷ Speed. km/h → m/s: × 5/18.

questions.questionText: Insert the bracket ( ) in the correct place, so that the equation will be true with respect to the BODMAS rule: 3 × 25 − 13 + 4 = 40
hints: Without brackets the answer is 66. Try each bracket and see which one gives 40.
Whatever is inside the bracket is calculated first.

questions.questionText: If 2x − 3 = 10, then what would be the value of 4x − 5?
hints: 4x is double 2x. Find 2x first, then double it.

questions.questionText: Find the number that divides 167 and 95 leaving 5 as remainder.
hints: If the remainder is 5, then 167 − 5 and 95 − 5 are exactly divisible by the number. Find their HCF. And the divisor must be bigger than 5.
Subtract the remainder first, then find the HCF.

questions.questionText: The length of a rectangle is twice its breadth. If the perimeter of the rectangle is 90 cm, find the area of the rectangle.
hints: If breadth = 1 part then length = 2 parts, so L + B = 3 parts. Half the perimeter gives L + B. Find one part first.
L + B = Perimeter ÷ 2. Area = L × B.

questions.questionText: When an article was sold for Rs.407 the shopkeeper makes a profit of 10%. What was the cost price of the article?
hints: A 10% profit means the selling price is 110% of the cost price. Find 1% first.
CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + Profit%).

questions.questionText: Arrange the given decimals in descending order of their values and find the sum of the 1st and the 4th: 0.062, 0.05, 0.56, 0.034, 0.007
hints: Write all numbers with 3 decimal places (0.050, 0.560 …) so they are easy to compare. Descending means biggest first.
Same number of decimal places makes decimals easy to compare.

questions.questionText: What sum of money will yield an interest of Rs.189 in 3 years at 9% p.a. simple interest?
hints: Use P = SI × 100 ÷ (R × T). First work out R × T = 9 × 3.

questions.questionText: If a = 3, b = 5 and c = b − a, then which of the following expressions has the greatest value?
hints: Find c first (b − a). Then put the numbers into each expression and compare the answers.
Substitution: find c, then replace every letter with its number.

questions.questionText: A man walks 900 metres in 18 minutes. How much distance would he cover in an hour?
hints: Find how far he walks in 1 minute. An hour has 60 minutes. Then change metres to km.
Unitary method: distance in 1 minute × 60. 1000 m = 1 km.

questions.questionText: The sum of two consecutive odd numbers is 16. Which equation from the following represents the given statement using 'm' as the variable?
hints: Consecutive odd numbers differ by 2. If one is m, the next is m + 2. 'Sum' means add.
Consecutive odd numbers: m, m + 2.

questions.questionText: A captain wants to arrange his soldiers in such a way that the number of soldiers in each row is the same as the number of rows. If there are 850 soldiers, how many soldiers will be left out?
hints: Rows × soldiers in each row with both numbers equal means a perfect square. Find the biggest perfect square that is not more than 850.
Biggest perfect square ≤ N, then N − that square = left over.

questions.questionText: Five persons consume 1 kg of rice in a day. Determine the amount of rice that will be consumed by 20 people in a week.
hints: 20 people is how many times 5 people? That tells you the rice for ONE day. A week has 7 days.
More people → more rice (direct proportion). 1 week = 7 days.

stepByStep.text: 20 ÷ 5 = 4, so 20 people eat 4 × 1 = 4 kg in a day.

questions.questionText: Where should the bracket ( ) be inserted in the given equation to make it true? 12 − 7 × 5 + 8 = 33
hints: Without brackets the answer is −15. Try each bracket and see which gives 33.
Whatever is inside the bracket is solved first.

questions.questionText: Which of the following fractions is equivalent to 36/54?
hints: Simplify 36/54 by dividing top and bottom by the same number (their HCF is 18). Then check the options.
Equivalent fractions: same value when simplified.

questions.questionText: The supplementary angle of an obtuse angle will always be:
hints: An obtuse angle is between 90° and 180°. Subtract it from 180° — what size range do you get?
Supplement = 180° − angle.

stepByStep.text: An angle less than 90° is an acute angle.

questions.questionText: In a basket 104 mangoes are there. If you take out 4 mangoes and replace them by 3 apples, till all mangoes are removed out of the basket, then how many apples will be there in the basket at the end?
hints: How many times can you take out 4 mangoes from 104? Each time puts in 3 apples.
Number of swaps = 104 ÷ 4. Apples = swaps × 3.

questions.subTopic: Grade 5 — Numbers (place value and number system)
questions.questionText: The 27th even number coming after 27 is?
hints: The first even number after 27 is 28. Then count up in 2s.
nth even number after an odd number o = (o + 1) + (n − 1) × 2.

questions.questionText: A five litre can of liquid soap costs Rs.370. What would be the cost of a three litre can of the same liquid soap?
hints: Find the cost of 1 litre first. Then multiply by 3.
Unitary method.

questions.questionText: If 40% of the students passed the exam, and the number of unsuccessful students were 420. How many students appeared for the exam?
hints: If 40% passed, what percent did NOT pass? 420 students are that percent.
Fail % = 100% − Pass %. Find 1% then 100%.

questions.questionText: How many three-digit numbers are there which are divisible by 4, 5 and 6?
hints: Find the LCM of 4, 5 and 6. Then list the three-digit multiples of it (first is 120).
Numbers divisible by all three are multiples of the LCM.

questions.questionText: An angle measures (35 − x)°, what will be the measure of the complementary angle of it?
hints: Complementary angles add to 90°. Subtract the whole bracket from 90 — watch the sign in front of x!
Complement = 90° − angle.

stepByStep.text: Open the bracket: 90 − 35 + x (the minus changes the sign of −x).

questions.questionText: Which of the fractions given below is the smallest?
hints: 7/6 is bigger than 1. For the others, see how far each is from 1: the biggest gap means the smallest fraction.
Gap to 1 = (denominator − numerator) ÷ denominator.

stepByStep.text: 7/6 is more than 1, so it's the biggest.
Gaps to 1: 11/12 is 1/12 short, 10/11 is 1/11 short, 21/22 is 1/22 short.
1/11 is the largest gap, so 10/11 is the smallest.

questions.questionText: Using the digits 2, 3, 4 and 5 each only once, all four-digit numbers are made. In how many numbers will the digit 5 be in the hundreds place?
hints: Put 5 in the hundreds place. Then count the ways to arrange the other three digits (2, 3, 4) in the remaining 3 places.
Arrangements of 3 different digits = 3 × 2 × 1 = 6.

stepByStep.text: The digits 2, 3, 4 fill the other three places.
First place: 3 choices, next: 2 choices, last: 1 choice → 3 × 2 × 1 = 6.

questions.questionText: Find the value of 'm' in the equation (m + 6)/11 = m/9
hints: Cross-multiply: multiply the top of the left fraction by 9 and the top of the right fraction by 11.
a/b = c/d → a × d = b × c.

questions.questionText: The area of a square and a rectangle are the same. If the side of the square is 15 cm, and the length of the rectangle is 25 cm, then the difference between the perimeter of the square and the rectangle is?
hints: Find the area of the square. Use it to find the rectangle's breadth (area ÷ length). Then find both perimeters and subtract.
Breadth = Area ÷ Length. Perimeter of rectangle = 2(L + B). Square = 4 × side.

stepByStep.text: Rectangle perimeter = 2 × (25 + 9) = 68 cm. Square perimeter = 4 × 15 = 60 cm.

questions.questionText: At a speed of 72 km/hr a car will cover a distance of 18 km in how much time?
hints: Time = Distance ÷ Speed. 18 ÷ 72 is a fraction of an hour. Change that into minutes.
Time = Distance ÷ Speed. 1 hour = 60 minutes.

questions.questionText: Given below are the sides of equilateral triangles and of squares in each of the alternatives. In which one does the perimeter of the equilateral triangle and the square become equal?
hints: Triangle perimeter = 3 × E. Square perimeter = 4 × S. Work both out for each option.
Equilateral triangle: 3 × side. Square: 4 × side.

stepByStep.text: Option D: 36 and 40 ✗. Answer: E = 16 & S = 12.

questions.questionText: A student scored 72% on a test of 25 questions. How many of his answers were wrong?
hints: First find how many he got right (72% of 25). The wrong ones are the rest. Careful: the question asks for WRONG.
Wrong = Total − Right.

questions.questionText: Simplify using the BODMAS rule: {(4 + 2 × 6) ÷ 4} − 4
hints: Do the inside bracket ( ) first — multiplication before addition. Then the { }.
Order: ( ) → { } , and inside brackets × before +.

questions.questionText: What decimal of an hour is 12 minutes?
hints: There are 60 minutes in an hour. Write 12/60 and change it to a decimal.
Decimal of an hour = minutes ÷ 60.

questions.questionText: The three angles of a triangle are x°, (x + 10)° and (2x − 6)°. Which one of the following is the greatest angle of this triangle?
hints: Angles of a triangle add up to 180°. Add the three angles and find x. Then work out each angle.
Angle sum of a triangle = 180°.

questions.questionText: A machine produces 150 toys in one minute. How many toys will it produce in 18 seconds?
hints: Find how many toys in 1 second (150 ÷ 60). Then multiply by 18.
1 minute = 60 seconds. Unitary method.

questions.questionText: Rearrange the digits of the number 75003064 to form the smallest number.
hints: The first digit can't be 0 (otherwise it isn't an 8-digit number). Put the smallest NON-zero digit first, then all the zeros, then the rest in increasing order.
Smallest number: smallest non-zero digit first, then 0s, then the others in ascending order.

questions.questionText: If Rs.3200 amounts to Rs.3680 in 3 years, then what is the rate of interest?
hints: Amount − Principal = interest. Then use R = SI × 100 ÷ (P × T).

questions.questionText: The H.C.F. of 513 and 456 is?
hints: Subtract: 513 − 456 = 57. The HCF divides 57 too. Test whether 57 divides both numbers.
HCF also divides the difference of the two numbers.

questions.questionText: The smallest number that can be added to 1325 to make the resulting number a square number is?
hints: Find the first perfect square above 1325. Try 36² and 37².
Next perfect square − the number.

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper bought a pen for Rs.40 and wishes to sell it at a profit of 25%. What price should he sell the pen for?
hints: 25% is one quarter. Find a quarter of 40 and add it to the cost price.
SP = CP + Profit.

questions.questionText: The three sides of a right-angled triangle are 9 cm, 40 cm and 41 cm. What is the area of this triangle?
hints: In a right-angled triangle the two shorter sides are the base and height. The longest side (41) is the hypotenuse — don't use it for the area.
Area of triangle = ½ × base × height.

stepByStep.text: Base = 40 cm and height = 9 cm (the two shorter sides).

questions.questionText: In the number 87459, how many times is the place value of 7 to that of 5?
hints: Find the place value of 7 (thousands place) and of 5 (tens place). Then divide.
Place value = digit × value of its place.

stepByStep.text: In 87459: 7 is in the thousands place → 7000. 5 is in the tens place → 50.

questions.questionText: At a college the number of girls are 735 which is 145 less than the number of boys in the college. If 435 boys and 375 girls are in the commerce stream, and the remaining in the science stream, then the number of students in the science stream are?
hints: Boys = girls + 145. Find the total students. Subtract the commerce students (435 + 375).
Science = Total − Commerce.

questions.questionText: Which will be the 8th term in the given series of numbers? 10, 12, 15, 20, 27, …
hints: Look at the gaps: 2, 3, 5, 7 … These are special numbers! What comes next in that list?
The gaps are prime numbers: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 …

questions.questionText: On Saturday afternoon Arnav sent 'm' text messages each hour for 5 hours and Pranav sent 'p' text messages each hour for 4 hours. Which of the following represents the total number of messages sent by Arnav and Pranav on Saturday afternoon?
hints: Messages = messages per hour × number of hours. Work out Arnav's total and Pranav's total separately, then add them.
Total for one person = rate × hours. Different letters can't be combined, so keep them apart.

questions.questionText: If 20% of an electricity bill is deducted, then Rs.100 is still to be paid. How much was the original bill?
hints: If 20% is taken off, what percent of the bill is left to pay? Rs.100 is that percent.
Whole = part ÷ percent × 100.

stepByStep.text: Left to pay = 100% − 20% = 80% of the bill = Rs.100.

questions.subTopic: Grade 5 — Numbers (place value and number system)
questions.questionText: If (x + 21) is an odd number, then find the 3rd even number coming after it.
hints: The first even number after an odd number is 1 more. After that, even numbers go up in 2s.
After odd number o: 1st even = o + 1, 2nd = o + 3, 3rd = o + 5.

questions.questionText: Which of the given expressions has the greatest value?
hints: Work out each expression with BODMAS: brackets first, then ×, then + and −.
BODMAS: B, then × before + and −.

questions.questionText: What is the complementary angle of the angle (x − 35)°?
hints: Complementary angles add to 90°. Subtract the whole bracket from 90 — be careful with the signs.
Complement = 90° − angle.

questions.questionText: A man earned Rs.120 when he sold 8 dozens of mangoes. How much would he earn if he sold 20 dozens of mangoes?
hints: Find the earning on ONE dozen first. Then multiply by 20.
Unitary method.

questions.questionText: The nine interior intersection points on a 4 × 4 grid of squares are shown (a 4 × 4 grid has 3 × 3 = 9 interior points). How many interior intersection points are there on a 16 × 16 grid of squares?
hints: A 4 × 4 grid has 3 lines inside each way, giving 3 × 3 points. How many inside lines does a 16 × 16 grid have each way?
An n × n grid has (n − 1) × (n − 1) interior points.

questions.questionText: A right-angled triangle has sides measuring 7 cm, 24 cm and 25 cm. Which of the following calculations could work out to be its area in sq.cm?
hints: The two shorter sides (7 and 24) are the base and the height. The longest side (25) is the hypotenuse and is NOT used for the area.
Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height.

questions.questionText: In April Harry bought a saddle for his horse for Rs.100. In May he sold it for Rs.200. In June he was sorry he had sold it, so he bought it back for Rs.300. In July he got tired of it, so he sold it for Rs.400. Which of the following is the true outcome of his transactions?
hints: Add up all the money he RECEIVED when selling and all the money he PAID when buying. Compare.
Profit = total money received − total money spent.

questions.questionText: Find the value of 'x' in the equation 3x + 7 = 1 − 2x
hints: Bring all the x terms to one side and the numbers to the other. Remember: when a term crosses the = sign, its sign changes.
Same operation on both sides.

questions.questionText: A fruit seller sells only apples (A), mangoes (M) and oranges (O). The total number of A and M with him are 400, the total number of M and O he has is 300, and the total numbers of A and O he has is 440. If he sells 100 fruits of each type, how many fruits of each type are remaining with him?
hints: Add the three pair-totals: you count every fruit type twice. Halve it to get the total of all fruits, then find each type.

stepByStep.text: After selling 100 of each: A = 170, M = 30, O = 70.

questions.questionText: In which of the numbers given below will the difference between the place values of the digits 9 and 7 be 83000?
hints: For each number find the place value of 9 and of 7, and subtract. You are looking for 83000.
Place value = digit × value of its place (ten-thousands = 10000, thousands = 1000 …).

questions.questionText: Three electronic bells beep after every 2, 5 and 8 minutes. If they all beeped together at 10:00 a.m., when will they beep together the next time?
hints: They beep together again after the LCM of 2, 5 and 8 minutes. Add that to 10:00 a.m.
LCM tells when repeating events coincide.

questions.questionText: In what time will Rs.25 become Rs.37 at 16% p.a. simple interest?
hints: Find the interest needed (37 − 25). Then find how much interest Rs.25 earns in one year at 16%.

questions.questionText: If 5/8 of the teachers of a coaching class plays chess, 3/8 teachers play carrom and 1/4 play both chess and carrom. What fraction of the teachers play neither of the two games?
hints: Those who play chess or carrom = chess + carrom − both (the 'both' group is counted twice). Then take it away from the whole (1).
Union = A + B − Both. Neither = 1 − Union.

questions.questionText: An ant moves 15 feet per minute. How many feet does it travel in 24 minutes and 40 seconds?
hints: Split the time: 24 minutes and 40 seconds. In 40 seconds the ant covers 2/3 of a minute's distance.
Distance = speed × time.

questions.questionText: Krina used her calculator and multiplied a number by 20 instead of by 2. What could she now do to obtain the correct answer?
hints: Her answer is how many times too big? Compare 20 with 2. Then do the opposite to fix it.
20 is 10 times 2. To undo ×10, divide by 10 (same as × 0.1).

stepByStep.text: Her answer = N × 20. The correct answer = N × 2.
20 ÷ 2 = 10 → her answer is 10 times too big.
Fix: divide by 10, which is the same as multiply by 0.1.

questions.questionText: If a/b = 2, what is the value of 4b/a?
hints: 4b/a is the 'flip' of a/b with a 4 on top. Flip 2 to get b/a, then multiply by 4.
If a/b = 2 then b/a = 1/2.

questions.subTopic: Grade 5 — Numbers (place value and number system)
questions.questionText: The sum of two consecutive prime numbers is 42. What is the difference of those two prime numbers?
hints: Each prime is close to half of 42 = 21. List the primes around 21 and find the consecutive pair that adds to 42.
Primes near 21: 17, 19, 23, 29.

stepByStep.text: Half of 42 is 21. The primes just below and above 21 are 19 and 23.
19 + 23 = 42 ✓ and there is no prime between them.

questions.questionText: A man takes up a work to be completed in 30 days for Rs.27000. He works for 18 days and then leaves. If you were the employer, how much would you pay him?
hints: Find the pay for ONE day (27000 ÷ 30). Then multiply by the 18 days he actually worked.
Unitary method: pay per day × days worked.

questions.questionText: Find the least number that must be added to 1300 so as to get a perfect square number.
hints: Find the first perfect square above 1300. Try 36² and 37².
Next perfect square − the number.

questions.questionText: Simplify using BODMAS: 778 − [5 + 3 of (25 − 2 × 10)]
hints: Inside the round bracket do 2 × 10 first, then subtract. 'Of' means multiply, and it comes before the + inside the square bracket.
BODMAS: Brackets (innermost first), Of, Division/Multiplication, Addition/Subtraction.

questions.questionText: The length and width of a rectangle are 12 cm and 8 cm respectively. Another rectangle whose area is the same as the first rectangle has length 16 cm. What could be the width of this rectangle?
hints: Find the area of the first rectangle. The second rectangle has the same area, so divide it by 16.
Width = Area ÷ Length.

questions.questionText: Ajay writes the sequence: 3, 14, 25, 36, … Which of the following numbers can appear in his sequence?
hints: The sequence goes up by 11 each time, starting from 3. Every term is 3 more than a multiple of 11. Check which option is 3 more than a multiple of 11.
Terms = 3 + 11 × (something). So (term − 3) must be divisible by 11.

stepByStep.text: Subtract 3 from each option and test divisibility by 11:

questions.questionText: The H.C.F. of 513, 1134 and 1215 is:
hints: Break each number into prime factors, or test each option: does it divide all three numbers?
513 = 3³ × 19, 1134 = 2 × 3⁴ × 7, 1215 = 3⁵ × 5. HCF = common prime factors.

stepByStep.text: Only the prime 3 is common to all three.
Smallest power of 3 in all of them = 3³ = 27.

questions.questionText: Kedar borrowed Rs.12000 from his friend at simple interest. He returned his friend Rs.15600 in full settlement of his loan after 5 years. What was the rate of interest charged by his friend?
hints: Rs.15600 is the amount (principal + interest). Subtract to find the interest. Then R = SI × 100 ÷ (P × T).

questions.questionText: A hospital stores one type of medicine in a 2-decagram container. How many 1-milligram doses are there in a 2-decagram container?
hints: 1 decagram = 10 grams. And 1 gram = 1000 milligrams. Change decagrams to grams, then to milligrams.
1 decagram = 10 g = 10,000 mg.

questions.questionText: What is 5% of 5% of Rs.100?
hints: Do it in two steps: first 5% of 100, then 5% of that answer.
'Percent of a percent': work out one step at a time.

questions.questionText: When a number X is divided by 5 the remainder is 2. When another number Y is divided by 5 the remainder is 4. When you divide X + Y by 5, then what should be the remainder?
hints: Pick real numbers: X = 7 (remainder 2) and Y = 9 (remainder 4). Add them and divide by 5.
Remainders can be added, then divided by 5 again.

stepByStep.text: Try X = 7 and Y = 9: X + Y = 16.

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper sold a bat for Rs.600 making a profit of 20%. What was the cost price of the bat?
hints: With 20% profit, Rs.600 is 120% of the cost price. Find 1% first.
CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + Profit%).

questions.subTopic: Grade 5 — Numbers (place value and number system)
questions.questionText: The sum of three consecutive natural numbers is 66. Which of the following can be one of the numbers of them?
hints: The middle number of three consecutive numbers is the average: 66 ÷ 3. Then find the numbers on either side.
Three consecutive numbers: (n − 1), n, (n + 1) — sum = 3n.

questions.questionText: Jack is reading a book whose pages are numbered from 1. The page numbers of the book have a total of 555 digits. How many pages are there in Jack's book?
hints: Count the digits in stages: pages 1–9 (1 digit each), pages 10–99 (2 digits each), then 3-digit pages. Subtract as you go.
Digits used: 9 × 1 + 90 × 2 = 189 up to page 99.

stepByStep.text: Pages 10–99: 90 pages × 2 = 180 digits. Total so far = 189.

questions.questionText: An insect flies at the rate of 10 m/sec. What is its speed in km/hr?
hints: To change m/s into km/h multiply by 18 ÷ 5 (or 3.6).

stepByStep.text: (In 1 hour = 3600 seconds, it flies 36,000 m = 36 km ✓)

questions.questionText: A man buys 1000 candy bars at a price of 5 for Rs.2. He sells all the candy bars at a price of 2 for Rs.1. What was his profit/loss percent?
hints: Find the total cost: 1000 bars in groups of 5 at Rs.2 each group. Then the total selling price: groups of 2 at Rs.1. Compare.
Profit % = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100.

questions.subTopic: Grade 5 — Numbers (place value and number system)
questions.questionText: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 11?
hints: Divisibility rule of 11: add the digits in the 1st, 3rd, 5th … places, add the digits in the 2nd, 4th, 6th … places, and subtract. The difference must be 0 or 11.
Test for 11: (sum of digits at odd places) − (sum of digits at even places) = 0, 11, 22 …

questions.questionText: What would be the 12th term of the series: 15, 19, 23, 27, …?
hints: Find the common difference. Then use nth term = first term + (n − 1) × d.
nth term = a + (n − 1) × d.

questions.questionText: An angle measures (25 − y)°. Which of the following is the complementary angle to this given angle?
hints: Complementary angles add up to 90°. Subtract the whole bracket from 90, and be careful with the minus sign.
Complement = 90° − angle.

questions.questionText: The digit 6 is used twice in the given numbers. Only at one number the place value of one 6 is 1000 times the other 6. Find it.
hints: Find the place value of each 6 in every option. You want one 6 to be worth exactly 1000 times the other.
Place value = digit × value of its place.

stepByStep.text: 68762: the first 6 is 60000 and the second 6 is in the tens place = 60 → 60000 ÷ 60 = 1000 ✓.

questions.questionText: If 2x + 1 = 8, then 4x + 1 = ?
hints: 4x is double 2x. First find 2x from the equation, then double it.

questions.questionText: If x = 3 and y = −2, then xy/(x − y) is:
hints: Put x = 3 and y = −2 in the top and bottom separately. Careful: x − y = 3 − (−2) = 3 + 2.
Substitute, then use the rules for negative numbers: minus × minus = plus.

questions.questionText: Which will be the 8th term in the given series of the numbers? 10, 12, 15, 20, 27, …
hints: Look at the gaps: 2, 3, 5, 7 … These are special numbers. What comes next?
The gaps are prime numbers: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 …

questions.subTopic: Grade 5 — Numbers (place value and number system)
questions.questionText: A number is perfectly divisible by 18. The number consists only of 4's. Example: 444 … What is the minimum number of 4's in this number?
hints: 18 = 2 × 9. A number made of 4s is always even, so the rule for 9 decides: the digit sum must be a multiple of 9.
Divisible by 9 → sum of digits is a multiple of 9.

stepByStep.text: The number ends in 4, so it is even (divisible by 2) ✓.
For 9: digit sum = 4 × (number of 4s) must be a multiple of 9.
4 and 9 share no factor, so the number of 4s must be a multiple of 9 → smallest is 9. (444444444)

questions.questionText: What least number should be subtracted from 13601, so that the remainder is divisible by 87?
hints: Divide 13601 by 87. The remainder is exactly the number you need to subtract.
Number − remainder is a multiple of the divisor.

questions.questionText: Which of the following numbers, when increased by 17, is equal to 60 times the reciprocal of the number?
hints: The reciprocal of n is 1/n. Test each option: add 17 and compare with 60 ÷ the number.
n + 17 = 60 ÷ n. Test the options.

questions.questionText: If one third of one fourth of a number is 15, then find the square of three tenth of that number.
hints: ⅓ of ¼ is 1/12. Find the number first. Then take 3/10 of it and square it.

questions.questionText: An aeroplane departs from Mumbai at 6:20 p.m. and reaches Dubai at 8:50 p.m. If the speed of the aeroplane is 212.5 m/s, find the distance between Mumbai and Dubai.
hints: Find the flying time and change it to seconds, because the speed is in metres per second. Then change metres into km.
Distance = speed × time. 1000 m = 1 km.

questions.questionText: Aniket borrowed Rs.18000 to open a grocery shop. He cleared off the loan by paying Rs.25,560 at the end of 3 years. Find the rate of interest.
hints: Rs.25,560 is the amount (principal + interest). Subtract to get the interest, then R = SI × 100 ÷ (P × T).
Solve each square bracket separately using its own common denominator (60 for the first, 90 for the second). Then divide: ÷ means × the flip.
First bracket LCD = 60. Second bracket LCD = 90. a ÷ b = a × (flip of b).

questions.questionText: What is the least number which should be subtracted from 0.000326 to make it a perfect square?
hints: 0.000326 has 6 decimal places, so think of it as 326 millionths. Which perfect square is just below 326? Then bring back the decimal places.
0.000326 = 326 ÷ 1,000,000. And 1,000,000 is itself a perfect square (1000²).

stepByStep.text: The perfect square just below 326 is 324 (18 × 18).
So the perfect square is 0.000324 (that is 0.018 × 0.018).

questions.questionText: A tailor has 37.5 metres of cloth and he has to make 8 pieces out of a metre of cloth. How many pieces can he make out of this cloth?
hints: Each metre gives 8 pieces. So multiply the number of metres by 8.
Pieces = metres × pieces per metre.

stepByStep.text: 300 is not among the first three options → None of these.

questions.questionText: The least number which when divided by 12, 15, 20 and 54 leaves in each case a remainder of 8.
hints: A number that leaves the SAME remainder with all divisors is: (LCM of the divisors) + the remainder.
Least number = LCM + remainder.

questions.questionText: One gross note book is bought for Rs.936. Find the cost of 48 books.
hints: One gross means 144. Find the cost of ONE book first, then multiply by 48.
1 gross = 12 dozen = 144. Unitary method.

questions.questionText: In the given series find the number in place of K: 9, 13, 21, 37, K, 133.
hints: Look at the gaps: 4, 8, 16 … Each gap is double the one before. Keep doubling to find K.
Gaps that double: 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 …

stepByStep.text: 69 is not among options A–C → None of these.

questions.questionText: What should be subtracted from 1015 to get the greatest three-digit square number?
hints: Find the greatest three-digit perfect square. 30² = 900, 31² = 961, 32² = 1024 (too big).
Greatest 3-digit square: the biggest square below 1000.

stepByStep.text: 32² = 1024 has 4 digits. 31² = 961 is the greatest 3-digit square.

questions.questionText: The simple interest earned on a certain principal at 8% p.a. in 5 years is Rs.160. What is the principal amount?
hints: R × T = 8 × 5 = 40, so the interest is 40% of the principal. If 40% = 160, what is 100%?

questions.questionText: Solve: 4(2x − 1) = 5(x + 2) + 4. Find the value of x.
hints: Open both brackets first (multiply each term inside). Then collect the x terms on one side.
Distribute: 4(2x − 1) = 8x − 4 and 5(x + 2) = 5x + 10.

questions.questionText: Find the sum of the squares of the greatest two-digit prime number and the smallest two-digit prime number.
hints: Greatest two-digit prime is 97 and smallest is 11. Square each, then add.

questions.subTopic: Grade 5 — Numbers (place value and number system)
questions.questionText: If (Z + 41) represents an even number, then which of the following represents the 19th odd number coming before it?
hints: Try a real even number, say 50. The odd numbers before it: 49, 47, 45 … Find the 19th and compare.
Before an even number e: nth odd number = e − 1 − (n − 1) × 2.

stepByStep.text: 19th odd number before e = e − 1 − (18 × 2) = e − 37.

questions.subTopic: Grade 5 — Numbers (place value and number system)
questions.questionText: How many odd three-digit square numbers are there in all?
hints: A square is odd only when the number being squared is odd. List the numbers whose squares have 3 digits: 10² = 100 up to 31² = 961.
Odd × odd = odd. 3-digit squares come from n = 10 to 31.

stepByStep.text: Count = (31 − 11) ÷ 2 + 1 = 11, which is not among options A–C → None of these.

questions.questionText: Which of the following fractions should be added to 2/5 to get 5/2?
hints: Subtract: 5/2 − 2/5. Use 10 as the common denominator.
Missing part = total − known part.

questions.questionText: An article worth Rs.400 is sold for Rs.324. Find the loss percent.
hints: First find the loss in rupees (CP − SP). Then loss % = loss ÷ CP × 100.
Loss % = (Loss ÷ Cost price) × 100.

questions.questionText: A train 120 metres long running with a speed of 36 km/hr will pass a pole in ____ seconds.
hints: Change 36 km/h to m/s (× 5/18). Passing a pole means covering its own length.
Time = Length ÷ Speed. km/h → m/s: × 5/18.

questions.questionText: Find the common number in place of each box (□): 15 7/17 + 10 (□)/17 + 7 (□)/17 + (□)/17 = 34
hints: Add the whole numbers first (15 + 10 + 7). Whatever is left to reach 34 must come from the fractions. Three boxes plus 7 over 17 …
Whole parts and fraction parts can be added separately.

stepByStep.text: Whole parts: 15 + 10 + 7 = 32. So the fractions must add to 34 − 32 = 2.

hints: Write the numbers under each other with the decimal points lined up and add zeros so every number has 3 decimal places.
Line up decimal points, then add like whole numbers.

questions.questionText: An 'MBA' student has to secure 40% marks to pass. He scores 94 marks and fails by 74 marks. Find the maximum marks.
hints: 'Fails by 74' means he needed 74 MORE marks. So the passing marks = 94 + 74. That is 40% of the maximum.
Whole = part ÷ percent × 100.

questions.questionText: The perimeter of a rectangle is 96 cm. If the breadth is 6 cm less than the length, find the area of the rectangle.
hints: L + B = half the perimeter. And B = L − 6. Put these together to find L, then B, then the area.
L + B = Perimeter ÷ 2. Area = L × B.
'Of' means multiply. Work out each 'of' first, add inside the bracket, then multiply by 2 and subtract.
BODMAS: Brackets, Of, then Division/Multiplication, then Addition/Subtraction.

questions.questionText: For Z = 7, which of the following equations is true?
hints: Put Z = 7 in BOTH sides of each equation. The equation is true only if both sides come out equal.
Substitution: replace Z with 7, then use BODMAS.

questions.questionText: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 13 and 1989 respectively. If one of the numbers is 221, then find the other number.
hints: HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers. Multiply 13 and 1989, then divide by 221.
HCF × LCM = First number × Second number.

questions.questionText: Mishti is facing south-west. She turns 180° in clockwise direction and then turns 225° in anti-clockwise direction. In which direction is she facing now?
hints: A 180° turn takes her to the opposite direction. Then count 45° steps anticlockwise: each step moves to the next direction (N → NW → W …).
Each 45° step = one direction (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW).

stepByStep.text: 225° ÷ 45° = 5 steps anticlockwise from NE: N, NW, W, SW, S.

questions.questionText: Where should the bracket ( ) be inserted to make the given equation true? 6 ÷ 21 − 9 × 36 + 11 = 29.
hints: Without brackets the answer is a big negative number. A bracket around a subtraction can make the divisor smaller. Try (21 − 9).
Whatever is inside the bracket is solved first.

questions.questionText: If Rs.26500 is deposited in a bank at 8% p.a. simple interest, what will be the amount at the end of 4 years?
hints: Find the interest first (P × R × T ÷ 100). The AMOUNT is the principal plus the interest.
Amount = P + SI.

questions.questionText: A two-digit number (♣8) is multiplied by a three-digit number (♣♣6). Which of the following can be their product if ♣ represents a digit, not necessarily the same?
hints: Check the last digit (8 × 6). Then check the smallest and biggest possible products to rule out the rest.
Smallest product = 18 × 106 = 1908. Largest product = 98 × 996 = 97,608.

stepByStep.text: Last digit: 8 × 6 = 48 → ends in 8. That removes 79764 (ends in 4).
1808 is smaller than the smallest possible product (1908) ✗.
970608 is bigger than the largest possible product (97,608) ✗.

hints: How did each number change? 6.7 → 0.67 is ÷ 10, and 58 → 5.8 is ÷ 10. So how does the answer change?
Dividing two factors by 10 each divides the product by 10 × 10 = 100.

questions.questionText: In the number sixty-seven lakhs, ninety-four thousand, five hundred and twenty-one, what is the place value of the digit which is exactly in the middle?
hints: Write the number in digits first: 67 lakhs = 67,00,000 … The number has 7 digits. Which one is exactly in the middle?
Place value = digit × value of its place.

stepByStep.text: The middle (4th) digit is 4. It is in the thousands place.

hints: Add the like terms together: all the w's, all the s's, all the r's — keep each sign with its term.
Combine like terms.

questions.questionText: (3a + 5), (7a + 10) and (4a + 15) are the sides of a triangle. For a = 5, what would be the perimeter of the triangle?
hints: Put a = 5 into each side. Then add the three sides.
Perimeter of a triangle = sum of its three sides.

questions.questionText: The perimeter of a rectangle is 84 cm. If the breadth of the rectangle is half of the length, find the length of the rectangle.
hints: L + B = half of 84. If B is half of L, then L + B is 1.5 times L.
L + B = Perimeter ÷ 2.

questions.questionText: A car travels 600 metres in 25 sec. How much distance will the car cover in 1 hour?
hints: Find the speed in metres per second. In 1 hour there are 3600 seconds. Then change metres to km.
Distance = speed × time. 1000 m = 1 km.

stepByStep.text: 86.4 is not among options A–C → None of these.

questions.questionText: A man buys a mobile phone for Rs.18000. He wants to make a profit of 18% on selling it. Find the selling price of the mobile phone.
hints: Find 18% of 18000 — that is the profit. Add it to the cost price.
SP = CP + Profit.

questions.subTopic: Grade 5 — Numbers (place value and number system)
questions.questionText: Find the sum of the numbers which are divisible by 3 of the following: 861, 435, 218, 764 and 1263.
hints: A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3. Test each number, then add only those that pass.
Divisibility rule of 3: digit sum is a multiple of 3.

questions.questionText: Find the 11th term of the given series: 19, 31, 43, 55, …
hints: Find the common difference. Then use nth term = a + (n − 1) × d.
nth term = a + (n − 1) × d.

questions.questionText: The sum of two consecutive odd numbers is 192. Which of the following equations represents the given statement using the variable 'W'?
hints: Consecutive odd numbers differ by 2. If the first is W, what is the next one? 'Sum' means add them.
Consecutive odd numbers: W and W + 2.

questions.questionText: What should be subtracted from the product of 13 × 14 to get the square of the smallest two-digit odd number?
hints: Smallest two-digit odd number is 11. Square it. Then work out 13 × 14 and find the difference.
Difference = product − square.

questions.questionText: 15% of 40 − 25% of A = 2. Find the value of A.
hints: Work out 15% of 40 first. Then ask: 6 minus what equals 2? That 'what' is 25% of A.
25% = ¼. If ¼ of A = 4, then A = 4 × 4.

questions.questionText: If 16 jugs can hold 1 decalitre of juice, how many jugs will be required to hold 15625 ml?
hints: 1 decalitre = 10 litres = 10,000 ml. Find how many ml ONE jug holds, then divide 15625 by it.
1 decalitre = 10 L = 10,000 ml. Unitary method.

questions.questionText: What is the sum of LCM and HCF of 12 and 90?
hints: Find the HCF (the biggest number that divides both) and the LCM (the smallest number both divide into). Then add them.

questions.questionText: What is the value of 1234 + 2341 + 3412 + 4123?
hints: Add column by column. Notice every column has the same four digits 1, 2, 3, 4 — what does each column add up to?
Each column: 4 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 10 (in some order).

stepByStep.text: Ones: 10 → write 0, carry 1. Tens: 10 + 1 = 11 → write 1, carry 1. Hundreds: 11 → write 1, carry 1. Thousands: 11.

questions.questionText: What is the value of y in: y − 3/4 = 5/12 − 1/3
hints: Solve the right side first (use 12 as the common denominator). Then move 3/4 across to the other side — its sign changes.
If y − a = b then y = b + a.

questions.questionText: Shraddha runs five rounds around a 400 m track in her school. For each round she runs the first 100 metres at 4 m/s and the remaining 300 m at 5 m/s. How much time did Shraddha take to complete the five rounds?
hints: Find the time for ONE round in two parts (time = distance ÷ speed). Add them, then multiply by 5 and change seconds into minutes.
Time = Distance ÷ Speed.

stepByStep.text: First 100 m: 100 ÷ 4 = 25 s. Remaining 300 m: 300 ÷ 5 = 60 s.
One round = 25 + 60 = 85 s. Five rounds = 85 × 5 = 425 s.
That is not among options A–C → none of these.

questions.questionText: The perimeter of a square is equal to the perimeter of a rectangle with length 22 m and breadth 16 m. Find the area of the square.
hints: Find the rectangle's perimeter first: 2 × (L + B). The square has the same perimeter, so divide by 4 to get its side.
Square: perimeter = 4 × side, area = side × side.
Work out the top (multiply) and the bottom (add) separately. The bottom is 1 + 2 + … + 8; use pairs to add quickly.
Sum of 1 to n = n × (n + 1) ÷ 2.

questions.questionText: What is the difference of LCM and HCF of 48 and 120?
hints: Find the HCF (biggest common factor) and the LCM (smallest common multiple). Then subtract: LCM − HCF.

questions.questionText: Z + 16% of 150 = 13% of 600. Find the value of Z.
hints: Work out the two percentages first: 1% of 150 is 1.5 and 1% of 600 is 6.

questions.questionText: What should be multiplied by the sum of 4/3 and 5/12, to get the final answer as 9/7?
hints: First add 4/3 and 5/12 (common denominator 12). Then ask: ? × (that sum) = 9/7. So ? = 9/7 ÷ (the sum).
If A × B = C then A = C ÷ B, and dividing by a fraction = multiplying by its flip.

questions.questionText: If Rs.6420 amounts to Rs.10,272 in 4 years at SI, then what is the rate of interest per annum?
hints: Amount − Principal = interest. Then R = SI × 100 ÷ (P × T).

stepByStep.text: 15% is not among options B–D → none of these.

questions.questionText: A clock is showing 12:45 pm now. When the hour hand has turned through 214°, what will the time be?
hints: The hour hand turns 30° each hour. How many hours and minutes is 214°? (0.5° each minute.) Then add to 12:45.
Hour hand: 30° per hour = ½° per minute.

questions.subTopic: Grade 5 — Numbers (place value and number system)
questions.questionText: If (M + 46) is a two-digit prime number, then find the 19th even number before it.
hints: A two-digit prime is odd. Try an example: if it is 51 (odd), the even numbers before it are 50, 48, 46 … Find the 19th and compare.
Before an odd number o: nth even number = o − 1 − (n − 1) × 2.

stepByStep.text: 19th even number before o = o − 1 − (18 × 2) = o − 37.

questions.subTopic: Grade 5 — Numbers (place value and number system)
questions.questionText: What is the product of all the one-digit factors of 48?
hints: List the factors of 48 that are less than 10, then multiply them all.
Factors of 48 below 10: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8.

questions.questionText: Find the value of (p + 3) × (p + 2) if 2p + 5 = 9p − 30.
hints: Solve the equation for p first (collect p terms on one side). Then put p into (p + 3) × (p + 2).
Same operation on both sides.

stepByStep.text: 56 is not among options A–C → none of these.

questions.questionText: 12 men can complete a work in 54 days. How many men will be required to complete the same work in 24 days?
hints: Fewer days means MORE men. Total work = men × days stays the same.
Men × Days = constant.

questions.questionText: Simplify using BODMAS rule: (9 + 3/5 of 25 − 7/13 of 39) ÷ 4/3
hints: 'Of' means multiply. Do both 'of' parts first inside the bracket, then add and subtract, then divide by 4/3 (multiply by 3/4).
BODMAS: Brackets, Of, then ÷ and ×, then + and −.

questions.questionText: The given series 26, 30, 34, 38, … is increasing by 4 each time. What will be the 59th term of the series?
hints: nth term = first term + (n − 1) × 4. Use (n − 1) = 58.
nth term = a + (n − 1) × d.

questions.questionText: The area of a right-angled triangle is equal to 18 times the base of the same triangle (numerically). Find the height of the triangle.
hints: Write area = ½ × base × height and set it equal to 18 × base. The base appears on both sides!
Area of triangle = ½ × base × height.

stepByStep.text: Cancel the base from both sides: ½ × height = 18.

questions.questionText: What fraction of a day is 216 minutes? (as a decimal)
hints: A day has 24 × 60 = 1440 minutes. Divide 216 by 1440.
Fraction = part ÷ whole.

questions.questionText: What principal amount will earn an interest of Rs.2205 in 12 months at 18% p.a. SI?
hints: 12 months = 1 year. So 18% of the principal is Rs.2205. Find 1% first.

questions.questionText: What number should be subtracted from the sum of 3042 and 869 to get a result of 2165?
hints: Add 3042 and 869 first. Then: that sum − (the number) = 2165, so the number = sum − 2165.
Missing number = sum − result.

questions.questionText: If 4x − 7 = 12, then what would be the value of 12x − 14?
hints: 12x is 3 times 4x. Find 4x first (4x = 12 + 7) — you don't need x itself.

questions.questionText: If a = 7, m = a − 2 and p = m + 5. Which of the following has the least value?
hints: Find m first, then p. Put the numbers into each expression and compare the three answers.
Find values in order: a → m → p.

questions.questionText: If an article is sold for Rs.336, the loss is Rs.84. Find the profit if the same article is sold for Rs.542.
hints: Loss = CP − SP, so CP = SP + Loss. Find CP, then compare it with Rs.542.
CP = SP + Loss. Profit = SP − CP.

stepByStep.text: 122 is not in options A–C → none of these.

questions.questionText: In how much time will Rs.450 become four times of itself at 24% p.a. SI?
hints: If the money becomes 4 times, the interest earned is 3 times the principal (4 − 1). Find the interest per year at 24%.
T = SI ÷ interest per year.

questions.questionText: A car travels 126 km in 12 litres of petrol. How many km will it travel in 22 litres of petrol?
hints: Find how far the car goes on just 1 litre, then multiply by 22.
Unitary method.

questions.questionText: Find the 10th term of the given series: 126, 124, 121, 116, 109, 98, …
hints: Look at the gaps going DOWN: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 … These are special numbers! Keep going with the same list.
